purpose: Bosentan is used to treat pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH), which is high blood pressure in the arteries that supply your lungs. It helps improve your ability to exercise and slows down the worsening of the condition. It can be used in adults and some children with this condition.
how_it_works: Your body naturally produces a chemical called endothelin that can cause blood vessels to tighten and narrow. In PAH, too much of this chemical makes the blood vessels in your lungs squeeze too tight, forcing your heart to work harder. Bosentan blocks the receptors that endothelin attaches to, allowing those blood vessels to relax and widen so blood can flow more easily.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include headache, flushing (feeling warm or red in the face), swelling in your legs or ankles, low blood pressure, and feeling tired. Some people also experience a stuffy or runny nose. Your liver enzymes may also rise, which is why regular blood tests are required.
warnings: Bosentan can cause serious liver damage, so you must have blood tests to check your liver every month. It must NEVER be taken during pregnancy because it can cause severe birth defects — reliable birth control is required for women who can become pregnant. It can also lower your red blood cell count (anemia). Bosentan can interact with many other medications, including hormonal birth control (making it less effective), so always tell your doctor and pharmacist all the medications you take.
typical_dosing: Adults usually start with 62.5 mg taken twice a day (morning and evening) for the first 4 weeks. After that, the dose is typically increased to 125 mg twice a day as a maintenance dose. The tablets should be swallowed whole and can be taken with or without food. Never stop taking this medication suddenly without talking to your doctor first.
